title: Supplier Payment
subtitle: Expense payable → voucher → GL, ledger and balances → reversal
summary: A payable is created when an expense is posted: single-branch expenses through Add Expense (spu_PostExpenseV2, PostingMode SINGLE), multi-branch ones through Expense Manual Multi-Branch (MULTI-MANUAL). Supplier Payment lists the supplier's open invoices (splist_Accounts). Submit takes a payment reference and a voucher number, then sp_PostSupplierPaymentWithManualLines calls sp_AddPaymentSupplierCompound_V2. Per invoice, V2 locks and re-reads the balance, settles it, posts a settlement ticket (one per branch share for multi-branch), writes the payment lines and a supplier-ledger debit; then one bank-recon line for the net cash and the cheque, cash or telegraphic voucher. Overpayments become supplier credit that a later voucher can apply. Supplier Voucher Reversal undoes a voucher with mirrored tickets and ledger rows.

keys.label: Supplier
keys.note: Supplier.SupplierID. ExpenseSummary / ExpenseMaster store it in SupplierID, TransactionPaymentAP and CheckVoucherCancelled in SupplierKey, SupplierLedger in both. On COREX001 SupplierKey = SupplierID for every supplier.

keys.label: Expense reference
keys.note: ReferenceNumber of the expense posting (ExpenseSummary / ExpenseMaster / its ticket / its ledger row). Balance-forward invoices loaded at go-live carry reference 1.

keys.label: Expense batch
keys.note: BatchReferenceID: with SupplierID + InvoiceNo, the key V2 uses to find and lock the invoice being paid. APPaymentDetails also stores it as SequenceReferenceNumber.

keys.label: Invoice
keys.note: The supplier's invoice number. The expense ticket stores it in ReferenceKey.

keys.label: Branch
keys.note: Which branch carries the expense line, ticket and payment share. A multi-branch invoice is paid per branch share, one ticket each.

keys.label: Payment reference
keys.note: ReferenceNumber from sp_GetReferenceNumber at Submit. Ties the voucher, payment lines, tickets, ledger rows, bank recon (SourceRef) and reversal audit together.

keys.label: Voucher no.
keys.note: VoucherID from sp_GetVoucherNumber. The payment ticket stores it in ReferenceKey, the bank recon line in ReferenceNo.

keys.label: GL ticket
keys.note: TicketNumber. APPaymentDetails.TicketNumber and SupplierLedger.TicketReference point back to it.

keys.label: Mnemonic
keys.note: SINGLE / EXP-MANUAL-CROSS-BR on expense tickets, SINGLE-PAY (single-branch) or EXP-ACCRUAL-PAY (multi-branch share) on payment tickets, PV-AP-* rows in JournalEntryMapping for overpay and advance accounts.

keys.label: GL account
keys.note: AccountCode. The bank account picked on the form is the voucher CreditGLCode, the payment line CreditGLCode, the ticket's credit leg and the bank recon AccountCode; the payable account (usually 20103) is the debit leg.

expTm.empty: No expense ticket: balance-forward invoices were loaded at go-live without one.

apd.role: Payment lines (per invoice / branch share / type)

credit.empty: This supplier has no overpayment or advance lines.

jem.empty: No overpay or advance on these vouchers, so no mapping row is read.

cvc.empty: No cancelled-cheque copy (not reversed, or not a cheque voucher).

steps.title: Expense is posted (the payable)
steps.where: Accounting › Add Expense · Expense Manual Multi-Branch
steps.what: Writes the payable to ExpenseSummary (Balance = what lands on the payable account), one ExpenseMaster row per debit line, the expense ticket and a supplier-ledger credit. For a PO-linked expense it also adds the inventory leg to Inventory.Cost (see the Item Costing Recon). Balance-forward invoices loaded at go-live have only the ExpenseSummary / ExpenseMaster / ledger rows.

steps.title: Voucher and payment lines are written
steps.what: The form sends the ticked invoices as dbo.AP_PaymentLineTVP (plus OverPay / Advance in dbo.AP_PaymentLineExtraTVP, and any manual debit lines). V2 writes the payment header, checks advance credit under an app lock (APCREDIT:supplier), then per invoice writes an EXPENSE PAYMENT line at gross and an OVERPAY / OVERPAYEXPENSE / ADVANCEAPPLIED line when used. Last, sp_Payment_CreateVoucherHeader writes the cheque, cash or telegraphic voucher for the net cash. The credit pool is the supplier's OVERPAY minus ADVANCEAPPLIED, skipping reversed vouchers.

steps.title: GL, ledger and balances are updated
steps.what: Per invoice (per branch share for multi-branch): reduce ExpenseSummary.Balance and set PARTIAL / FULLYPAID, settle ExpenseMaster, post the settlement ticket (DR payable, CR bank, CR EWT / discount, DR/CR the overpay or advance account from JournalEntryMapping) and debit the supplier ledger. After the loop, one OC bank-recon line for the total net cash. The ledger trigger recomputes SupplierAccounts.

steps.title: Voucher is reversed
steps.what: Refuses a voucher whose overpayment credit a later voucher already used (60519). Flags the voucher, writes the audit row and a cancelled-cheque copy, restores each invoice's balance, tags the ledger rows and adds mirror credits, copies each payment ticket with DR/CR swapped (Product = REVERSAL), and resolves the bank-recon line as VOIDED. The wrapper then flags the cash / telegraphic voucher too.

scenarios.title: Cheque paying one single-branch expense
scenarios.story: A Cagayan petty-cash replenishment posted through Add Expense (4 expense lines, one SINGLE ticket), paid in full by one cheque. Follow the batch and invoice keys from the payable to the payment line, then the payment reference and voucher number through the ticket, ledger and bank recon.

scenarios.title: Multi-branch expense: one invoice, three branch shares
scenarios.story: A Cebu petty-cash replenishment split across branches 002, 013 and 888. Payment writes one payment line and one settlement ticket per branch share, with one voucher and one bank-recon line for the total. Note the expense side: all three branch tickets share ticket number 7239.

scenarios.title: Overpayment credit applied, reversed, applied again
scenarios.story: Voucher 735 settles two invoices and overpays one by 2.00 (OVERPAY, carried as supplier credit). Voucher 736 applies that 2.00 to the next invoice (ADVANCEAPPLIED) and was later reversed as a wrong entry, which returned the credit; voucher 737 then applied it to the same invoice again. The credit pool table shows the running story.

scenarios.title: Cash voucher reversed
scenarios.story: A cash voucher paying a customs expense, reversed the next day for a wrong date. The cash voucher has no cancelled-cheque copy; it is flagged by the reversal wrapper instead of by sp_CancelledChequesCS.

findings.title: Single expenses' ledger rows point to a ticket that doesn't exist
findings.text: spu_PostExpenseV2 posts the expense ticket under the @TicketNumber the form passed in, but writes SupplierLedger.TicketReference from a second, new GetTicketNumber call. On COREX001 all 379 SNGLE ledger rows reference a ticket number that has no TicketMaster row, and every expense burns one ticket number. Fix: use @TicketNumber for TicketReference and drop the extra GetTicketNumber call.

findings.title: Invoice payment and manual debit lines aren't one transaction
findings.text: sp_PostSupplierPaymentWithManualLines calls V2 (which commits) and then sp_PostCashAdvance. If the manual lines fail, the invoice payment stays posted; the proc's own error message tells the user not to re-run it. The final voucher-amount and bank-recon corrections are also outside any transaction.

findings.title: The 'already reversed' guard only looks at CheckVoucher
findings.text: sp_CancelledChequesCS refuses a second reversal only when CheckVoucher.isErrorCorrect = 1. For cash and telegraphic vouchers the flag is set afterwards by sp_ReverseCombinedSupplierVoucher, which itself has no transaction. A second call for a cash or telegraphic voucher (or a failure between the two procs) would pass the guard and reverse it again. Guard on PaymentReversalAudit instead, and wrap the wrapper in a transaction.

findings.title: Multi-branch expense tickets share one ticket number
findings.text: sp_PostExpenseManualMultiBranch gets one ticket number before its branch loop, so every branch's ticket header carries the same TicketNumber (7239 in the multi-branch sample), while sp_EditExpenseManualMultiBranch and the payment side use one number per branch. Already in the work log as an open question.

findings.title: Reversal tickets look like normal payment tickets
findings.text: sp_ReverseTicketsAP copies the original Status (POSTED) and Mnemonic; only Product = 'REVERSAL' and the '(REVERSAL)' prefix in Particulars mark them. A report that filters tickets by Mnemonic sees both and nets them to zero, which is right, but one that lists POSTED payment tickets will show the reversal as a payment.

findings.title: Column names don't say which supplier key they hold
findings.text: V2 matches ExpenseSummary.SupplierID against Supplier.SupplierKey, while APPaymentDetails.SupplierID and the reversal procs use Supplier.SupplierID, and PaymentReversalAudit.VoucherType holds the pay method (EXPENSE / PURCHASE), not CHECK / CASH. On COREX001 SupplierKey = SupplierID for all 138 suppliers, so nothing breaks today; a supplier created with different values would stop matching.

findings.title: Not traced yet: PURCHASE mode
findings.text: Paying PO purchases (APAccounts, PV-AP mnemonics through sp_PostCompoundTicket) is a separate branch of V2. COREX001 has only 3 such vouchers; it can be added as its own sample once there's a representative one.
